## Overview

We will focus on using generative AI (genAI) tools to help you with tasks in
omics data analysis, especially coding tasks.

## Learning goals

This week you will learn:

#### Lecture A: [Generative AI: tools, prompts, and pitfalls](./w8a_genAI.qmd)

- Basic background of generative AI (genAI) and large language models (LLMs)
- About Ohio State's genAI tools, and genAI use in this course and in research
- How chat-based and agentic AI differ
- Example prompts and outputs with Gemini, including Deep Research
- How to write effective prompts
- Tips and pitfalls when using genAI, especially for coding
- What to use (and not use) genAI for, and why it rewards expertise

#### Lecture B: [Coding with an AI agent in VS Code](./w8b_claude.qmd)

- Setting up and using the Claude extension in VS Code Server at OSC
- Using Claude to ask questions about, write, and edit code
- Letting Claude act as an "agent" that runs commands,
  and controlling what it may do with permission modes
- Giving Claude persistent instructions (ones that carry over between conversations) with a `CLAUDE.md` file
- Managing Claude's context window and costs
